plain_description.what: Tests a product rule: decline to declare one model better than another in a cell when the answer key itself does not clearly separate them. It is applied on three leaderboard views, and the test counts how many calls are lost and how many wrong separations are removed. No judge calls.
plain_description.why: It asks whether a simple key-based rule removes the remaining wrong 'model A beats model B' claims without giving up too many correct ones.
plain_description.information: Low cost with most errors removed would make it worth shipping. Losing more than 25% of calls would make it too blunt. Result: undetermined on the registered criterion, because the target count referred to a board that no longer exists. On the existing board the rule is cheap and works. Combined with the widener it leaves 0 wrong separations on the pooled board while still calling about 150 of 190 pairs. The per-cell residue is 4 to 5 errors in 1,714 calls depending on the random seed, all involving one model (Llama-3.1-70B). The failure condition did not fire. Older judged question family, later ruled 'history, not evidence'.
